answer: A Sybil-resistant AI-agent economy can use a stake-and-slash identity bond: before an agent may vote or earn, it locks real collateral, and any two accounts traced to one funding source forfeit it. Every clone therefore needs fresh capital. Growing from an ember of one fake account into a zephyr of thousands burns the attacker's wallet, and a single detected link toasts the whole stake. At the zenith of such an attack, buying influence costs more than earning it honestly, so minting identities stops paying.
